key_insight: GeRo enables Vision-Language-Action models to jointly plan and generate language-grounded future traffic scenes via autoregressive rollouts, turning VLA models into generative planners rather than only imitators.
problem_solved: Addresses reliance on sparse trajectory annotations and under-utilization of VLA models' generative potential, improving multi-step planning, scene forecasting, and scenario coverage for end-to-end autonomous driving.
method: Plug-and-play GeRo wrapper that autoregressively rolls out future timesteps: at each step the VLA model generates both language-grounded scene descriptions and next actions.
Joint planning + generation loop uses generated scenes to inform subsequent action predictions, creating richer supervision and longer-horizon forecasts beyond sparse trajectories.
Language grounding of generated scenarios enables interpretable scene variations and supports scenario augmentation for robustness testing and training.
impact: Provides a practical way to turn VLA models into generative planners that produce interpretable, inspectable future scenarios—improving data efficiency, generalization, and safety analysis for autonomous driving research and deployment.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: sensor input -> VLA model -> autoregressive rollout loop producing paired language-scene + action at each timestep
Timeline/rollout visualization: stacked frames showing generated future scenes and associated actions across multiple timesteps
Before vs after: comparison of sparse imitation-only training vs GeRo-generated scenario augmentation improving coverage
Icon/legend set: language bubble (scene description), car icon (action), timeline arrow (rollout), shield/check (safety/robustness)
paper_title: Generative Scenario Rollouts for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
paper_authors: Rajeev Yasarla, Deepti Hegde, Shizhong Han, Hsin-Pai Cheng, Yunxiao Shi
